question: Should OpenClaw adopt this public plugin SDK, Gateway protocol, and durable approval-attempt contract as the supported provider-agnostic external-verification seam, subject to successful live completion proof?
rationale: The RFC is described as design-accepted, but this PR turns that direction into a large, compatibility-sensitive public and persisted contract that cannot be safely accepted from contributor implementation evidence alone.

options.title: Sponsor the generic seam
options.body: Confirm the API and ownership boundary, then require inspectable successful completion and upgrade proof before merging.

options.title: Narrow the contract first
options.body: Ask for a smaller internal or experimental seam if maintainers do not want the current plugin API, protocol, and persistence commitments.

options.title: Defer core support
options.body: Keep the canonical tracker open and pause this PR until a maintainer commits to the permanent external-verification product direction.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the generic seam
recommendation.body: Confirm the API and ownership boundary, then require inspectable successful completion and upgrade proof before merging.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied canonical tracker attributes acceptance of the underlying RFC design to Kevin.
